item.text: I’ve got enough to synthesize without more searching. The evidence cluster is clear: strong positives on peaceful transfer, free speech, and civil-rights enforcement, with meaningful negatives around surveillance and protest policing, but no sign of internet shutdowns or outright democratic rollback.

**Bottom line**
Biden looks **slightly stronger overall on 4B.10** than he inherited the office, but only modestly and unevenly. The strongest positives are his acceptance of electoral transfer, repeated defense of free speech and press freedom, and federal civil-rights enforcement. The main counterweights are surveillance authority, allegations of platform pressure, and a coercive protest-policing climate. I found **no reliable evidence of U.S. internet shutdowns** in 2024.

| Assessment | Title | Publisher | Date | URL | Claim-level summary | IDs |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---|---|
| Positive | Address to the Nation on the 2024 Presidential Election | The American Presidency Project / White House | 2024-11-07 | https://www.presidency.ucsb.edu/documents/address-the-nation-the-2024-presidential-election | Biden congratulated Trump, said power changes through peaceful elections, and directed his administration to cooperate on an orderly transition. This is direct evidence that he accepted constitutional transfer and did not try to entrench himself. | 4B.8, 4B.10 |
| Positive | Biden drops out of 2024 race after disastrous debate, inflamed age concerns, VP Harris gets his nod | Associated Press | 2024-07-21 | https://www.ap.org/news-highlights/elections/2024/biden-drops-out-of-2024-race-after-disastrous-debate-inflamed-age-concerns-vp-harris-gets-his-nod/ | Biden exited the race and endorsed Harris under party pressure rather than clinging to the ticket. That is indirect but relevant evidence that succession stayed inside normal rules. | 4B.8, 4B.10 |
| Positive | Statement on World Press Freedom Day | The American Presidency Project / White House | 2024-05-03 | https://www.presidency.ucsb.edu/documents/statement-world-press-freedom-day-8 | Biden said the free press is essential and that journalism should not be criminalized. This supports a stronger political-freedom environment for scrutiny and dissent. | 4B.6, 4B.10 |
| Positive | Remarks on Political Protests at College Campuses and an Exchange With Reporters | The American Presidency Project / White House | 2024-05-02 | https://www.presidency.ucsb.edu/documents/remarks-political-protests-college-campuses-and-exchange-with-reporters | Biden explicitly defended free speech and peaceful assembly while rejecting authoritarian suppression of dissent. That is direct support for unpopular viewpoints being legally protected. | 4B.7, 4B.10 |
| Positive | Biden denounces resurgence of Islamophobia amid Gaza war | Reuters via ThePrint | 2024-03-15 | https://theprint.in/world/biden-denounces-resurgence-of-islamophobia-amid-gaza-war/2002734/ | Biden condemned Islamophobia, anti-Palestinian bias, and antisemitism and said Muslims and Arabs deserve dignity and equal rights. This is direct evidence for protecting minority political equality. | 4B.7, 4B.10 |
| Positive | Justice Department finds civil rights violations in Phoenix Police Department and City of Phoenix | U.S. Department of Justice | 2024-06-13 | https://www.justice.gov/archives/opa/pr/justice-department-finds-civil-rights-violations-phoenix-police-department-and-city-phoenix | DOJ found unconstitutional policing and discriminatory enforcement against Black, Hispanic, and Native American people, including people engaged in demonstrations. That supports a reading of federal willingness to correct local abuse rather than tolerate it. | 4B.4, 4B.7, 4B.10 |

This is the clearest direct counterevidence on privacy and political-freedom limits. | 4B.9, 4B.10 |

This is allegation-level counterevidence for digital pressure, not a merits finding. | 4B.6, 4B.9, 4B.10 |
| Negative | Police were advised to avoid mass arrests, then came the US campus protests | Reuters via Investing.com | 2024-05-10 | https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/police-were-advised-to-avoid-mass-arrests-then-came-the-us-campus-protests-3433913 | Mass arrests across dozens of campuses despite advice to avoid that approach show a coercive protest climate and weaker protection for unpopular views in practice. | 4B.7, 4B.9, 4B.10 |

**Search gap**
- I found no credible evidence of actual U.S. internet shutdowns in 2024 attributable to Biden.
- The strongest negative material is about surveillance authority, platform-pressure allegations, and protest policing, not a full authoritarian shutdown model.
- I did not find strong evidence that Biden reversed term limits or tried to block an electoral transfer; the evidence on succession points the other way.

**Overall judgment**
- **4B.10: slightly stronger than inherited, but only modestly**
- The case for “stronger” rests on protected transfer, institutionalized civil-rights enforcement, and repeated public defense of speech and press.
- The case against comes from surveillance authority and coercive handling of protest and online speech, which meaningfully blunt the strength of the positive record.
